units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:1">Ab. Zar. III, 1</cite> <he>כל שיש בידו … או צ׳ וכ׳</he> a statue which holds in its hand a staff or a bird &c.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 41a:4">Ib. 41ᵃ</cite> <he>צ׳ שתופש … כצ׳</he> the emblem of the bird is a symbol that he causes himself to be caught like a bird in behalf of the entire world (v. <cite ref="K00118"><he>כַּדּוּר</he></cite>); Y. ib. III, 42ᶜ bot. <he>צ׳ ותמצא וכ׳</he> the bird alludes to (<cite ref="Isaiah 10:14">Is. X, 14</cite>), ‘My hand reacheth forth, as for a nest, to the riches of all peoples’ (universal conquest); <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13:15">Num. R. s. 13</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 13:5">Sabb. XIII, 5</cite>, v. <cite ref="R00161"><he>צוּד</he></cite> h.
<cite ref="Shabbat 106b:5">Ib. 106ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>צ׳ דרור</he>, v. <cite ref="D01075"><he>דְּרוֹר</he></cite>; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:2:17">Y. Snh. X, 28ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>אמר לו אין צִפּוֹרְךָ מדינית</he> (some ed. <cite ref="R00684"><he>צִפּוֹרָה</he></cite>) he said to Moses, is not thy bird (Zipporah) a Midianite?—

<cite ref="Mishnah Makhshirin 5:2">Makhsh. V, 2</cite> <he>העושה צ׳ במים</he> (Var. <cite ref="R00613"><he>צִנּוֹר</he></cite>) if one makes ‘a bird’ in water (producing bubbles by blowing through a tube); <cite ref="Tosefta Makhshirin 2:13">Tosef. ib. II, 13</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="R00416"><he>צִפּוֹרִים</he></cite>, <he>צִפֳּרִים</he>, <he>רִין …</he>, <cite ref="R00030"><he>צִי׳</he></cite>.

Naz. I, 1 הרי עלי צ׳ וכ׳ (Y. ed. צפר׳) if a person says, I vow birds …, he is bound to be a Nazarite; Y. ib. 51ᵃ bot., sq. ציפורין. Ib. וכי צ׳ הוא מביא וכ׳ does the Nazarite offer ‘birds’, does he not offer doves &c.? Ib. כל עוף … קרוי צ׳ all birds, whether clean or unclean, are called tsipporin. Bab. ib. 3ᵃ ציפרין סמוכין לשיער וכ׳ in saying, ‘I vow birds’, he presumably had in his mind the birds mentioned in connection with the growth of hair (Dan. IV, 30).
<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 14:1">Neg. XIV, 1</cite> <he>צִפֳּרֵי דרור</he> (Mish. ed. <he>צפרים</he>), v. <cite ref="D01075"><he>דְּרוֹר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 29a:8">Ab. Zar. 29ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 57b:16">Ber. 57ᵇ</cite> <he>בשר צ׳</he> birds’ flesh (bad for convalescents); a. fr.

senses.gloss: צ׳ נפש (צִפָּר נ׳, צִי׳) [‘the bird of life’,] the cartilage at the end of the sternum (cartilago ensiformis).
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 90b:15">B. Kam. 90ᵇ</cite> <he>במה הכהו</he> … <he>ציפור נפשו</he> Ms. R. (ed. <he>כמה … ציפר נ׳</he>; Ms. F. <he>צפר</he>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40) wherewith he struck him, and whether he struck him on his leg or on his stomach; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 331:1">Yalk. Ex. 331</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Sanhedrin 12:3">Tosef. Snh. XII, 3</cite>. Tosef. Macc. V (IV), 15 <he>כדי שלא תגיע לציפר וכ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>לצפור</he>; <he>לצורפי</he>, cler. error for <he>לציפור</he>) lest the whip reach his stomach, and he die.—<he>צ׳ כרמים</he>, v. <cite ref="R00688"><he>צִפּוֹרֶת</he></cite>.—[<he>צפור</he>, <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 4:14">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. IV, 14</cite> ed. Zuck., v. <cite ref="R00698"><he>צְפִירָא</he> II</cite>.]
